criteria.rationale: Verified that preview and apply use the same catalog adoption implementation and date input: adopt.go:127-139 and configuration_review.go:435 onward. Policy maps are freshly decoded and preview does not publish them. The focused regression passed. R2's explanatory branch has no direct automated test, as the spec acknowledges; its defaults and command were checked against the catalog and CLI parser. Full validation reruns timed out, so their success is not assumed. No new accepted risk is asserted.
The added work mutates local decoded maps only. It introduces no goroutines, shared mutable state, cancellation ownership or lifecycle changes; publication remains in the existing apply path.
The CLI adds the specified adopt.change and adopt.values output. Request identity, answers, pair-flag refusal, file schemas and MCP contracts remain unchanged.
Existing request validation and pair-flag rejection remain active. The new policy-load failure returns a contextual failure and exit code 1; no new unbounded input processing is introduced.
Checked configuration-review requests, setup consumers, catalog adoption and existing adoption effects. Broader relevant tests passed across domain, CLI, MCP-server and scaffold packages.
Preview now reports catalog changes through the established adopt.change field. Policy-load errors include actionable context; the added explanation contains no secret material.
Compared request and direct adoption paths. The change adds the output promised by the spec without altering stored policy formats, request authority, adopted values or public MCP interfaces.

The focused regression command passed independently. Broader selected tests also passed in all four affected supporting packages. Catalog change descriptions are produced before existing adoption-effect descriptions, and preview remains non-publishing.

R1's cause was omission of catalog policy changes from the request preview. adopt.go:127-139 invokes the same catalog function used by apply on independently loaded maps, avoiding duplicate policy-setting logic. R2 adds the alternative-values command beside those changes. R3 corrects attribution in the distributed prose. No individual structural facts requiring mappings were listed in the brief.

Inspected all four manual diffs. English and Portuguese root/scaffold copies consistently attribute the qualified sandboxed Claude profile to pose-dist, preserving the surrounding operational instructions.

The closeout catalog produces the explicit never/never changes, and adopt.values names the complete direct command and allowed values for choosing alternatives. Existing request and policy failures retain contextual errors.

R1 is covered by the independently passing preview/apply regression and shared catalog implementation. R2 was verified against adopt.go:136-137, the closeout catalog defaults and CLI usage. R3 was verified in all four manual copies and distribution-related tests. The constraint refusing pair flags remains tested.

The scoped implementation is a small preview-only addition, a regression test, validation registration and four attribution edits. Apply semantics and parametrized request answers remain outside this change, as required by the non-goals.

Inspected the scoped diff and request-to-policy path. No new command execution, dependencies, credentials, path construction or authority changes were introduced. Preview changes only local decoded maps; existing request validation and guarded publication remain responsible for apply.

Reusing the catalog's existing adoption function is the smallest sufficient way to keep preview descriptions aligned with writes. A separate planner or duplicated key list would add unnecessary contracts. The change adds no speculative abstraction. This choice would need reconsideration if catalog adoption acquired external side effects or stopped returning complete change descriptions.
